Split documents into sentences, clauses, or phrases

Source: R/segment.R
segment.Rd

segment() splits documents into sentences, clauses, or phrases by deterministic rules, with no model involved, so the result is reproducible and needs no download. A long document usually discusses several things, and one embedding of the whole document averages them; shorter units can each be embedded and assigned to a topic on their own, so that a document can be described as a mixture of topics, and each unit stays within the input length of the model.

The "sentence" level splits at ., ? and !, protecting the periods of abbreviations (see abbreviations()), decimal numbers and parenthetical remarks. The "clause" level, the default, also splits at ;, :, spaced dashes, and subordinating words such as "which", "where" or "in terms of", while comma-separated lists stay whole. The "phrase" level also splits at commas. Quotes, dashes and whitespace are normalized first; letter case is kept. Optional steps merge very short segments into their neighbors, cap segment length at a number of words or model tokens, and drop segments with little alphabetic content, such as citation fragments. The result is a data frame with one row per segment.

The topic verbs segment documents themselves through their segment argument (see topics() and topic_corpus()); call segment() directly to inspect the units, or to reuse one segmentation and its embeddings in topic_gamma() and blend().

Usage

segment(
  text,
  level = c("clause", "sentence", "phrase"),
  merge_below = 0L,
  abbreviations = default_abbreviations(),
  cores = 1L,
  max_tokens = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  min_content = 0
)

Arguments

text

Character vector of documents. Names are carried into the document_name column.

level

"clause" (default), "sentence", or "phrase".

merge_below

Join segments shorter than this many words to a neighbor; 0 (default) keeps every segment as split.

abbreviations

Abbreviations, each ending in a period, whose period never ends a sentence (default abbreviations()); matched ignoring case.

cores

Number of forked processes used to split documents (default 1). Ignored on Windows and for small inputs; the result does not depend on it.

max_tokens

Maximum length of a segment, or NULL (default) for no limit. A longer segment is split again at clause words, ;, :, dashes or commas, or, failing those, before a function word near the limit. Length is counted in words, or in the tokens of model when one is given; a tokenizer yields more tokens than words, so a word limit should sit below the model's token limit.

model

NULL (default), or a model from load_model() whose tokenizer counts the length for max_tokens. Requires max_tokens; splitting then runs in one process.

min_content

Minimum share of alphabetic content, between 0 and 1, for a segment to be kept (see content_ratio()); 0 (default) keeps every segment.

Value

A base data frame with one row per segment and columns document_id (position of the document in text), document_name (its name, or ""), segment (position within the document), and text. Blank documents contribute no rows.

Conditions

sbert_bad_input when model is given without max_tokens.

See also

abbreviations() for the protected abbreviations; content_ratio() for min_content; topics() and topic_corpus(), which segment through their segment argument; topic_gamma() and blend(), which take this data frame.

Examples

feedback <- c(
  first = paste("The task was clear. I liked the colors, the sounds",
                "and the pictures, which were funny."),
  second = "Too hard; I did not understand the question."
)
segment(feedback)
#>   document_id document_name segment
#> 1           1         first       1
#> 2           1         first       2
#> 3           1         first       3
#> 4           2        second       1
#> 5           2        second       2
#>                                               text
#> 1                              The task was clear.
#> 2 I liked the colors, the sounds and the pictures,
#> 3                                which were funny.
#> 4                                        Too hard;
#> 5               I did not understand the question.
segment(feedback, level = "sentence")
#>   document_id document_name segment
#> 1           1         first       1
#> 2           1         first       2
#> 3           2        second       1
#>                                                                 text
#> 1                                                The task was clear.
#> 2 I liked the colors, the sounds and the pictures, which were funny.
#> 3                       Too hard; I did not understand the question.
segment(feedback, level = "phrase")
#>   document_id document_name segment                               text
#> 1           1         first       1                The task was clear.
#> 2           1         first       2                I liked the colors,
#> 3           1         first       3       the sounds and the pictures,
#> 4           1         first       4                  which were funny.
#> 5           2        second       1                          Too hard;
#> 6           2        second       2 I did not understand the question.

# Abbreviation and decimal periods do not end a sentence.
segment("See Fig. 3 for details. The mean was 2.5 points.",
        level = "sentence")
#>   document_id document_name segment                     text
#> 1           1                     1  See Fig. 3 for details.
#> 2           1                     2 The mean was 2.5 points.
